div.head: Erc 1
div.ab: . . . ‘Anno dominicae incarnationis DCXL Eadbald rex Cantuariorum transiens ex hac uita Earconbercto filio regni gubernacula reliquit, quae ille suscepta XXIIII annis et aliquot mensibus nobilissime tenuit. Hic primus regum Anglorum in toto regno suo idola relinqui ac destrui, simul et ieiunium XL dierum obseruari, principali auctoritate praecepit. Quae ne facile a quopiam posset contemni, in transgressores dignas et competentes punitiones proposuit.’ . . .

In the year of the Lord’s incarnation 640, Eadbald, king of the people of Kent, passing from this life, left the helm of the kingdom to his son Earconberht; and he, having taken it up, held it most nobly for twenty-four years and some months. He was the first of the kings of the English to command, by his sovereign authority, that idols be abandoned and destroyed throughout his whole kingdom, and at the same time that the fast of forty days be observed. And that this might not easily be scorned by anyone, he laid down deserved and suitable punishments against transgressors.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 9 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page); Liebermann’s heading: EARCONBERHT.; Source as Liebermann gives it: Aus Baedae Historia ecclesiastica gentis Anglorum III 8.; F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date at the head of the text); Wormald, Making of English Law I; Whitelock, English Historical Documents I, October 2026 (was “640–664 (Liebermann)”, now “640–664 (Liebermann, I p. 9)”)

note.seg: Text aus A. Holder’s 2. Ausgabe, welche der Hs. Cambridge Univ. Kk V 16, um 737 geschrieben, folgt. Keine Variante ergab der Vergleich mit J. Stevenson’s Ausgabe (1838) und mit der H. Petrie’s in Monum. hist. Britann. (1848).

Text from A. Holder’s 2nd edition, which follows the MS Cambridge Univ. Kk V 16, written c. 737. Comparison with J. Stevenson’s edition (1838) and with H. Petrie’s in Monum. hist. Britann. (1848) yielded no variant.
-brecto Hs. Namur 8. Jhs., fränkisch; -berhto Hs. Tiber. C II, Ende 8. Jhs. Laut Sweet, Oldest Engl. texts, p. 138.
-brecto MS Namur, 8th cent., Frankish; -berhto MS Tiber. C II, end of the 8th cent. According to Sweet, Oldest Engl. texts, p. 138.

Das Jahr wiederholt Beda V 24; 640 Eodbald filius Edilberti depositus 13 Kal. Febr., feria 6 Ann. Juvav. maiores in Mon. Germ., SS. I 87. Der 20. Jan. 640 war aber Donnerstag. Den 22. Jan. gibt der späte Kenter Thorne n Hist. Anglic. SS. X., 1769

Beda V 24 repeats the year; 640 Eodbald filius Edilberti depositus 13 Kal. Febr., feria 6 Ann. Juvav. maiores in Mon. Germ., SS. I 87. But 20 Jan. 640 was a Thursday. The late Kentish writer Thorne gives 22 Jan., in Hist. Anglic. SS. X., 1769

Dass er 664 am 14. Juli starb, sagt Beda III 27. IV 1. V 24.—Dass hier wirkliche Gesetze gegen Heidentum (s. d. Gl 4f.) und Bruch der Fasten (s. d. Gl 1f.) zugrunde liegen, nimmt auch Stubbs an; Councils III 92. Vielleicht benutzte sie Wi 12—15.— Eine Beistimmung der Witan (s. d. Gl 13), obwohl unerwähnt, ist durch Beda nicht ausgeschlossen; ihr Fehlen widerspräche dem regelmässigen Zustandekommen der Gesetze; s. d. Gl 15

That he died on 14 July 664 is stated by Beda III 27. IV 1. V 24.—That real laws against heathenism (see that word in Gl 4f.) and breach of the fasts (see that word in Gl 1f.) underlie this is also assumed by Stubbs; Councils III 92. Perhaps Wi 12—15 used them.— An assent of the witan (see that word in Gl 13), though not mentioned, is not ruled out by Beda; its absence would contradict the regular way in which laws were enacted; see that word in Gl 15
